title: ECM/PCM Processor Internal Fault (Extended)
shortDescription: PCM internal fault — internal CPU watchdog or RAM error.
fullDescription: This is an internal control module fault flagged after the extended self-test. Internal cpu watchdog or ram error. These codes typically require module reprogramming or replacement, but should be confirmed by ruling out power, ground, and external short conditions first.
safetyImpact: Module faults can cause loss of drivability, unintended acceleration mitigation, or no-start.

causes.cause: Corroded ECM connector or water intrusion
Low or unstable battery voltage during operation

fixSteps.title: Check Battery and Charging
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm battery is healthy (12.6 V resting, 13.8–14.7 V running). Many internal-ECM codes are caused by undervoltage events.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ECM Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect ECM connectors and inspect for corrosion, bent pins, or water marks. Service the connectors before condemning the module.

fixSteps.title: Check Power & Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all ECM power feeds and grounds with a voltage drop test under load.

fixSteps.title: Reflash or Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Attempt a software reflash through a dealer or capable scan tool. Replace and program the ECM if reflash fails or hardware fault is confirmed.

faq.a: Not always. Connector and ground issues mimic ECM failure. Diagnose carefully before spending on replacement.

faq.q: Can I install a used ECM?
faq.a: Most modern vehicles immobilizer-pair the ECM to the keys — used modules require dealer programming or won't start the engine.

title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit (Extended)
shortDescription: Reference voltage / driver output fault for intake air heater control circuit.
fullDescription: Code P0640 flags a fault on a PCM-driven reference voltage or actuator output circuit. Several sensors typically share each reference, so a short on one sensor can disable an entire group of inputs and trigger this code.
safetyImpact: Multiple sensor inputs may default to substitute values, degrading drivability and emissions monitoring.

causes.cause: Sensor on shared reference shorted internally
Wiring chafed to ground or power

symptoms: A/C, glow plug, or warning lamp inoperative

fixSteps.title: Scan All Sensor Data
fixSteps.instruction: Capture live data for all 5V reference circuits and identify which sensors share the affected reference bus.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect Sensors One-by-One
fixSteps.instruction: With key on, disconnect each sensor on the shared 5V circuit while watching scan data — when the short clears, the offending sensor is identified.

fixSteps.title: Measure Reference at Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Probe the reference pin at each connector with a multimeter. Should read 4.9–5.1 V key-on, engine-off.

fixSteps.title: Repair Wiring or Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Repair shorted/chafed wiring. If the reference voltage cannot be restored at the ECM connector with all sensors disconnected, the ECM has an internal fault.

faq.q: Why do I have several sensor codes at once?
faq.a: Sensors share 5V references in groups of 3-5. A short on one disables the whole group and sets multiple codes.
Less than 10% of the time. Always rule out shorted external sensors and wiring first.

fixSteps.instruction: With key on, disconnect each sensor on the shared 5V circuit while watching scan data — when the short clears, the offending sensor is identified.

fixSteps.instruction: Probe the reference pin at each connector with a multimeter. Should read 4.9–5.1 V key-on, engine-off.

fixSteps.instruction: Repair shorted/chafed wiring. If the reference voltage cannot be restored at the ECM connector with all sensors disconnected, the ECM has an internal fault.

faq.q: Why do I have several sensor codes at once?
faq.a: Sensors share 5V references in groups of 3-5. A short on one disables the whole group and sets multiple codes.
Less than 10% of the time. Always rule out shorted external sensors and wiring first.

fullDescription: Code P0670 flags a fault on a PCM-driven reference voltage or actuator output circuit. Several sensors typically share each reference, so a short on one sensor can disable an entire group of inputs and trigger this code.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open (Extended)
shortDescription: Power relay or cooling fan driver fault — ecm/pcm power relay sense circuit open.
fullDescription: Code P0688 indicates a fault on a PCM-controlled relay or fan driver output. Short to power, short to ground, open circuit, or a stuck relay can all trigger this code. On cooling-fan circuits, ignoring the code risks engine overheating.
safetyImpact: Cooling fan failure can cause engine overheating in slow traffic; main relay sense issues can cause stalling.
symptoms: Vehicle stalls or won't restart hot

fixSteps.title: Check Fuses and Relays
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the underhood fuse box. Pull and inspect the relevant fuse and relay; swap with a known-good identical relay.

fixSteps.title: Command the Output
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scan tool to command the relay or fan on. Listen for the click and confirm operation.

fixSteps.title: Measure Driver Output
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe the ECM driver wire while the output is commanded — should switch to ground or 12V depending on circuit type.

fixSteps.title: Repair / Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed relay, fan motor, or repair wiring. Confirm fix with bidirectional command and a road test.

faq.a: If the cooling fan is affected, do not drive in traffic — engine overheating can ruin the head gasket. Otherwise schedule prompt service.
Use OEM or known-quality brands — cheap relays are a frequent repeat-failure source.
